rationale.conceptual: The method requires genuine domain knowledge: generating special quasirandom structures, DFT calculations with proper settings, post-processing to compute local Lagrangian strain tensors and an equivalent strain metric defined in the paper, and implementing a geometric-elastic model derived in the appendices. This goes beyond off-the-shelf use of a single library; it involves a non-trivial, multi-part algorithm unique to the material.
rationale.execution: The pipeline is multi-stage (~7 distinct steps) with strong dependencies: generating SQS supercells, five pure-element calculations, volume relaxations for 11 alloys, full relaxations for 11 alloys, elastic constant computations for 11 alloys, strain analysis, and theoretical model calculation. Orchestration requires installing and combining ATAT and Quantum ESPRESSO, managing intermediate files, and handling many similar but distinct runs. This is a long, fragile orchestration though data handling is minimal.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires understanding and implementing a custom analytical model for lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys and performing a full DFT workflow for 11 alloys and 5 pure elements. The conceptual complexity is high due to the need to correctly generate SQS structures, run DFT volume and full relaxations, compute elastic constants, extract local strain tensors, and implement the paper's own theoretical model. The execution pipeline is long and fragile, involving multiple sequential stages and external tools (ATAT, Quantum ESPRESSO), but the compute requirements are entirely CPU-based and moderate in memory.

compute_estimate.reasoning: All calculations are DFT-based, run entirely on CPU; no GPU is used. Peak memory per individual run is typical for plane-wave DFT on ~120-atom cells (~32–64 GB). Total input data (pseudopotentials, SQS structures) is under 1 GB. The reference runtime estimate is ~55 CPU-hours.
